subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: How can understanding personal readiness and goal design help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

prompts.prompt: Explain movement screening without diagnosis in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, quotation, data display, map, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of warm-up design.
Apply skill baseline in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite evidence.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, or design flaw involving activity preferences; correct it and explain why.
Connect movement screening without diagnosis with safety and recovery plan. Explain how the ideas support, constrain, contrast with, or build on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Create an individualized participation plan based on safe progress and enjoyment rather than comparison.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
